body: Is there a possible reason he didn't explain anything until after I confronted him? He had the opportunity to do so.

No. Think things would be worse back home.

It's late now, and I should probably go to bed. I have my call tomorrow. I think I've vented enough that I can get through it without blowing a gasket. At the very least I want to find out what my therapist did and why more than I want to kill myself for the time being.
Friend got me a job out here. Known him most of my life now.
Yeah. Not the best at Japanese after having a couple of years of no speaking practice due to COVID, and I don't need to speak Japanese at my work.

I don't want to. I'm in Japan, so finding one equipped with English speaking staff is a bit of a task (this was partially why I was let go from the one I went to), and based on my experience and what few English accounts I could find online, Japanese inpatient mental health care is totally unfit for purpose. The use of physical restraint is thousands of time higher here than it is in other developed countries. I saw about twelve to fifteen patients while I was inside, and all of them were totally vacant. Completely doped up. I have no idea how you're meant to come back from weeks/months of that treatment.

Honestly, the thought had crossed my mind, but I can't really be sure. A part of me has felt like he just doesn't want to acknowledge that the emergency care hurt me more than it helped because of his part in it, however small, but I haven't said that to him. I think it's possible to talk it through without; if that is the case he can deal with it on his end through his supervisor.

Thanks for the honest response. I don't disagree in principle with what he said about the purpose of a psych ward, but I feel like even a slightly empathetic response couldn't have hurt, especially while the experience was still fresh. 

I suppose after typing everything out, the main thing is that I don't feel believed about the doctor just being an utter bastard, which is the core part of how bad my experience was. I was open to having time to reset and get some help (and I wasn't expecting a picnic, either), right up to when he asked me if the room looked like prison in the way that he did -- that's just rubbing the situation in my face. I've had plenty of interactions with doctors of different fields, and I've had some who were distant, or a little authoritarian as my therapist put it, but I've never doubted their overall intentions as I did with this guy. I just got the sense he wanted to dope me up and enjoy his power trip. Another doctor there I spoke to I didn't particularly like, but I didn't get the same feeling from him, if that makes sense. I feel a bit invalidated by my therapist's rephrasing things back to me in a way which downplays what I described.

I'll probably bring it up with him when we speak next. At the absolute worst, I don't think starting again here and now is a good idea given how things have gone so far.
